language.howToChooseYourGradeIntro: Our curriculum Grades K to 6 corresponds with ages:
language.howToChooseYourGradeContent:
It’s very important children start at the right level, have fun in learning and work at their own pace. Please help the children selecting the level that is not too easy, but also not too difficult for them. There are two ways to do this.

  • You can either check the learning goals yourself to determine the correct level for your child(ren).
  • Or you can let the child take several lessons to determine his or her level. For example, if your child has the age of 6, please let him or her take one lesson in grade K, one lesson in grade 1, and one lesson in grade 2 to determine at which level he or she is.
language.lessonRating: How do you feel about this exercise?

dialog.text: Hello, my name is Chip!
Hi, I'm Dolly! I live in Australia in a big place called Sheep Central.
Today, we're counting how many sheep we have. I've asked my nephews to help me!
I've asked Nephew Blue to count ones, Nephew Green to count thousands and Nephew Red to count millions.
Nephew Blue will count sheep until he gets to a thousand.
Then, he ands over the group to Nephew Green and starts over.
Nephew Green only counts groups. He now has one group of a thousand sheep.
Nephew Green gets more and moe groups of a thousand sheep from Nephew Blue.
When Nephew Green gets to a thousand groups, he hands over his groups to Nephew Red.
Finally, Nephew Red counts his groups as well. Each of his groups is called a million.
Can you help us count our sheep?

It gets even more complicated! Some sheep can only read Roman numerals. Can you help us figure out the right amounts?
Remember, when a small numeral comes before a big numeral you have to subtract them. For example, XI means 11, but IX means 9. Good luck!
